FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

Mainz know they will get dragged further into the Bundesliga’s relegation battle if they slip up against a Union Berlin side who already sit inside the bottom two.

Match News and Current Form

Under-pressure manager Urs Fischer branded Mainz’s defending as “slapstick” as a 3-1 defeat to Augsburg last time out signalled their worst run of form in six years. The club have now lost five matches in a row across all competitions, and with four of those coming in the league, they have sunk to just three points above the relegation zone going into this round. Form at the Mewa Arena is a major concern, with the 05ers one of only three teams in the division yet to win on home soil this term (D1, L4), but confidence can be drawn from going unbeaten against teams who head into this round below them in the table (W2, D1). 

Union Berlin remain in the bottom two after their 5-1 thrashing at the hands of RB Leipzig last weekend. That was already the fifth league game this term in which the club have conceded 3+ times, so it's no surprise they enter this round having conceded a joint-Bundesliga high of 26 goals. To make matters worse, Mauro Lustrinelli’s men have now gone six matches without success across all competitions (D3, L3), while no team in the division has picked up fewer than their one point on the road (D1, L3), scoring a league-low of one goal in the process.

Head-to-Head History

After a 3-1 defeat in the corresponding fixture last season, Mainz are on a ten-match winless run against Union Berlin (D4, L6).

Opta by StatsPerform
Hot Stats and Streaks

Only has committed more Bundesliga fouls on Mainz pre-round (124).

Mainz’s 23 offsides are the second most in the Bundesliga ahead of this round.

Union Berlin have received a pre-round joint-league high 26 yellow cards.

No team in the division has had fewer shots than Union Berlin’s 105 this season.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

No player has picked up more Bundesliga yellow cards than Mainz’s Phillipp Mwene this season, while he has also been booked in three of his nine H2Hs. Janik Haberer is unbeaten across the eight Union Berlin games in which he has scored (W6, D2), with six of his nine strikes during that period serving as the first or last of the game.

Dominik Kohr and Silas remain sidelined for Mainz. Union Berlin’s Zeno Van Den Bosch is suspended, while Livan Burcu and Josip Juranović missed the RB Leipzig defeat.

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.

Betting Analysis

Two leaky defences are coming face-to-face, meaning value might be found in both teams to score and over 2.5 goals.

Author: Matt Jones
